# Pele1.9 component wrapping: static novelty and observability review

**The specific new idea is opt-in disconnected Class wrapping to an explicit display width. It is not a new solver or evidence of faster cyclic layout.** Our current source already packs/separates some component-like units. I did not find the same final Class row-wrap policy in EC72, but saved public Class layouts omit enough painted geometry that a complete offline packing qualification is not currently justified.

No metric, render, product parser, source modification, build or cost run was performed. The peer sources were retrieved read-only at e7f092a4de147cc32210913c20e36eaa5fcd0ef1; our source references below are pinned EC72.

## What Pele actually implements

[components.ts](https://github.com/obsidianmd/pele/blob/e7f092a4de147cc32210913c20e36eaa5fcd0ef1/src/layout/components.ts) is72 lines, Git blob01d52d54ac8e04186a959811d3641c06842ea756. It joins both parent containment and every edge, preserves original component encounter order, includes node rectangles, route coordinates and edge-label boxes in component envelopes, and translates whole components into rows separated by a gap. A proposal is applied only when its resulting width is narrower; the helper alone does not promise smaller area or lower height.

The actual caller matters. [Class render.ts469–478](https://github.com/obsidianmd/pele/blob/e7f092a4de147cc32210913c20e36eaa5fcd0ef1/src/diagrams/class/render.ts#L469) invokes it only when a positive explicit options.maxWidth is exceeded. Endpoint cardinalities become temporary parented CNodes at471, so they contribute bounds and move with their endpoint's component; coordinates are copied back at474. Main self-loop label anchors are established before wrapping. [shiftLayout373](https://github.com/obsidianmd/pele/blob/e7f092a4de147cc32210913c20e36eaa5fcd0ef1/src/layout/compound.ts#L373) owns the common translation. This is a Class display-budget feature, not evidence that every Pele family/default graph is repacked.

## Existing EC72 mechanisms and distinction

| Existing owner | What is already present | Difference from the proposed Class feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ER separateErCompounds](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/er/layout.ts#L617) | Builds sibling connected components and compound items, moves them together to resolve collisions/label/terminal clearance. Route reconstruction preserves complete producer paths when both endpoints translate equally at428. | Existing family-specific component packing; not an explicit max-width shelf wrap. Do not claim component translation itself is new. |
| [Architecture constraints](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/architecture/layout.ts#L600) | Unions fixed-axis row/column components, orders/moves whole units and separates compounds while retaining authored alignment. | A generic weak-component wrapper could violate these semantics. Outside this Class-only proposal. |
| [Measured forest](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/layout/measured-forest.ts#L44) | Places roots side by side in subtree spans with shared depth bands; shared by native and the qualified indexed forest path. | Already separates multiple roots, without width-limited row wrapping. It is an active qualified path, not unused code to delete. |
| [Compound native placement](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/layout/agentic-compound-core.ts#L69) | Places scopes bottom-up and translates owned leaves, groups, routes and labels into parent coordinates. | Coordinate projection/compound layout, not a final display-width packing policy. |
| [Class ELK adapter](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/class/layout.ts#L191) | Layered ELK with namespaces, orthogonal routes, labels and spacing. | ELK can already arrange disconnected pieces internally; absence of our own wrapper does not establish an unpacked comparator. Study only extra benefit over the final saved layout. |
| [Shared epilogue](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/layout-engine.ts#L1680) | Route/label/note passes, global nonnegative translation and final canvas expansion. | Global translation preserves shape but does not rearrange components. Final bounds deliberately retain clearance and earlier dimensions; tight envelope area is not automatically the current canvas area. |

The source search and targeted prior report/history queries found no earlier exact experiment for Class width-limited disconnected wrapping. This is bounded negative search evidence, not proof that every historical archive or abandoned branch has been inspected. Rejected rank, compaction, endpoint and text-allocation candidates are different mechanisms; their failures neither prove nor disprove this idea.

**Our current API does not expose Class maxWidth.** [RenderOptions.class](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/types.ts#L570) contains hierarchicalNamespaces only. maxWidth exists for Kanban and Timeline with different documented behavior. wrappingWidth is Flowchart text wrapping. componentSpacing is explicitly extension-defined with **no built-in consumer** in [render-contract268](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/render-contract.ts#L268). None may silently be reinterpreted as a new global or Class packing option.

## What must travel together

A safe part is a closure over every Class relationship, self-loop and namespace parent/member relationship. A connected pair may never be split. Include note-for attachment or conservatively decline unknown standalone-note ownership; preserve namespace hierarchy and empty namespace boxes. Stable order follows authored identity order, never a score-selected permutation.

Each translated part must include class surfaces/interface occurrences, annotation/member/header text, all namespace frame/header text, complete route geometry/control/rounding authority, relationship labels and halos, both endpoint cardinalities and their halos, marker overlays, self-loop label/attachment geometry, and notes plus both note connector endpoints. [Class title translation711](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/class/layout.ts#L711) demonstrates the otherwise easily missed note targetY/noteY and cardinality fields. A diagram title is global chrome with its own width/band/alignment: it cannot be attached to the first component or cropped after wrapping.

Envelope bounds must account for actual retained text, marker extents, strokes/joins/caps, transforms and paint uncertainty, not just node rectangles and polyline vertices. Translation mathematically preserves internal paths and angles, but floating-point addition can change stored differences; old geometry certificates/output digests cannot be reused as proof of a changed output. New inter-component/global-chrome collisions must be checked after proposing offsets.

## Saved-data feasibility

The existing EC72 captures bind final source, SVG, complete receipts, public debug layout and original full-value/V8 payloads. They are useful for identity/topology, main route geometry, main label rectangles and group envelopes. They do not persist the typed PositionedClassDiagram or complete native paint primitive inventory.

[projectClassPositioned1–52](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/positioned-views/class.ts#L1) exports classes, relationships/main labels and namespaces, but omits notes, endpoint cardinality anchors and the diagram title. The typed fields exist in [class/types.ts148–260](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/ec72a06dcf57d1e429fab9672a9acbf794e22d9f/src/class/types.ts#L148). Even complete public roundtrips therefore do not recover every positioned painted object. Generic graph projection likewise omits state notes.

PaintLayoutCertification retains counts/issues/status/viewport, not all primitives/owner bounds. A passed certificate proves the original output, not a complete data table from which new part bounds can be reconstructed. Regions and SVG IDs are not substitutes for missing prepared text/marker/connector authority. SVG text alone is not an invitation to add another incomplete parser, especially while471 owns shared XML/CSS/bounds work.

Thus a **public-envelope-only** offline screen is feasible, but must be labeled partial and cannot establish complete painted area/label/group safety. A trustworthy full42-Class proposed-offset result requires complete owned positioned/paint observations, or an independently justified proof that a particular case needs none of the missing geometry. Missing/unknown evidence is a retained decline, never inferred absence.

## One finite protocol proposed for root review

See PROPOSAL.json. Scope is the root-nominated existing42 matched Class sources, both saved native/ELK outcomes and both cache policies. Freeze their immutable ordered IDs/source/capture hashes before any geometry result. No generated cases, fresh render, outcome-based subset, parameter search or production change.

Use one diagnostic display budget800px, original40px Class padding and40px gap (not a new public option). Preserve encounter order. Emit symbolic per-component dx/dy instead of mutating original artifacts. All42 entries remain in the output, including single-component/no-op, typed failure, unverified or unobservable cases. Do not run the packing metric stage until the complete-ownership gate is satisfied; otherwise report the observability limitation.

If that gate is met, report original/proposed width, height, canvas/tight-paint area and aspect ratio separately, all component membership/offsets, route length/bends, label/group overlap and global-title clearance. Require narrower width **and no area increase**, complete identity/ownership closure and no new collision/lost enclosure before calling a geometric proposal admissible. Preserve every adverse case; do not widen the budget or reduce the safety envelope to find wins. A large component may remain wider than800 as a best-effort result, not be scaled.

Apply the same diagnostic policy separately to both native and ELK saved layouts. An improvement over one native layout is not proof of native superiority to an equally repacked ELK result. No inference of solver speed, allocation, RSS, viewer usability or final SVG/receipt fidelity follows from offline area. A future product option would require separate API design, actual source-bound final rendering/certification and payload/cost qualification.

Current decision: worthwhile as a narrowly scoped Class observability/geometry hypothesis; **not ready to execute a full-paint metric experiment from public layouts alone, and no implementation is authorized**.

# Four-worker VM activity diagnostic — proposal only

No capture is declared or authorized by this document. No runtime, maintained benchmark worker, original target or prior result changes. Root must review before implementation/freeze/execution.

The baseline-only calibration failed despite all24 workers/10800 full public calls completing. Its worst native/OFF pair has whole75 wall ratio2.474710 and processCPU ratio2.457222. That pair changes direction across its six passes: warm wall ratios.567682/.613841, then.687460/2.744522/1.749425/4.931265. Existing records therefore reject the claim that the declared extra warmup established stable performance. They neither identify GC/JIT nor establish an exclusively external waiting explanation. ProcessCPU includes process threads and is not wall or main-thread CPU.

## One finite design

Use four fresh workers on the accepted ec72 canonical artifact05b105b1 only. Fixed order: native/OFF1, native/NORMAL1, native/NORMAL2, native/OFF2. This deliberately selects the failing native workload as a diagnostic witness while retaining both cache policies and two independent processes per policy. It does not diagnose ELK or claim that native is uniquely unstable. All original ordered75 inputs remain, including every H27 family, D48 case and edit workflow; exact original full SVG/receipt oracles and options are mandatory.

Each worker executes the already-frozen2-warmup/4-timed whole75-pass schedule:450 fully consumed public API calls,1800 across all four workers. It is an instrumented activity observation, not another calibration or C2-T candidate test. No A/A acceptance statistic, candidate enrollment, adaptive warmup, shortened population, forced GC, JIT-disabling/heap-size intervention or automatic retry exists.

Operational limits are120seconds per worker and480seconds SHARED by all four workers, including launch/reap/bookkeeping. All four slots must be persisted before the first launch, running persisted before Popen, and every failed/timeout/unlaunched slot retained. If instrumentation cannot finish this exact schedule within the bounds, record incomplete; do not reduce passes, suppress events or retry to obtain a prettier trace.

## Instruments and command shape

Use pinned actualNode24.19 and a NEW external evaluator, not a patched renderer or maintained worker. Reuse the frozen measuredCall consumption function and source-bound invoke/workflow/options/payload/oracle logic. Every SVG/complete receipt UTF8 payload and final-source hash must exactly match the accepted baseline oracle, with the original one final callback and inherited paint limitations retained.

Pinned V8 source places GC scopes under v8 and optimization/compilation scopes under disabled-by-default-v8.compile. ## Predeclared questions and analyses

1. **Is foreground GC pause time a material component of captured slow envelopes?** Parse actual event names/categories/thread IDs; retain unknowns. Pair begin/end events per PID/TID, clip to call envelopes and compute interval UNION, so nested MinorGC/MajorGC/V8.GC scopes are never added twice. Main-thread GC wall coverage is distinct from concurrent background elapsed spans and processCPU. Report every call/pass, all raw events and unmatched spans. A captured slow envelope with tiny foreground-GC coverage rules out a foreground-pause-only accounting explanation for that envelope; it does not rule out background-GC CPU, allocation effects or GC's influence on JIT.

2. **Does compilation/tiering activity persist into late captured passes?** Report main-thread and background compile/optimization/deopt events separately, with names/counts/interval unions and late-pass location. Join main-thread CPU frame samples only where clock mapping is admitted. Late activity contradicts assuming that this captured process finished compilation after warmup; event coincidence does not prove it caused the wall variation. No events is not proof of stable tiers or absence of deoptimization.

3. **Where is the remaining sampled main-thread work?** Report complete worker-level self/inclusive stacks, foreground GC/compile interval unions and uncategorized main-thread spans. Include parsing, layout, normalization, proof, SVG/receipt materialization and observer stacks where actually identified. Unknown frames stay unknown; no anonymous core frame is relabelled an entire specific algorithm. Profile weights are samples, not exact invocation/allocation counts. A non-covered wall remainder is accounting residue, not a corrected 'GC-free renderer time'.

For organization only, prospectively flag envelopes >=2times the six-call median for the same input in the same worker. Keep all450 calls regardless of that flag. Flag foreground-GC coverage>=25% and foreground compile coverage>=10% as material activity, and foregroundGC<10% on a flagged slow envelope as insufficient for a pause-only accounting explanation. These are descriptive accounting labels, not significance tests or renderer acceptance targets. Compute overlap unions and report overlaps separately; do not add GC and compile spans blindly.

Collect low-impact PID/PPID, current-mm RSS/heap metadata and cgroup cpu.max/cpu.stat before and after EACH whole75 pass, outside API envelopes. Keep exact sample times. Shared cgroup counters remain contextual and cannot be attributed to the renderer or subtracted from timings. Per-process maxRSS is retained only as a lifetime observation in light of the completed8-probe RSS experiment. Cache-key activity, CPU frequency, scheduler steal, instruction counts and allocator traffic are not measured by this plan.

## What this can and cannot decide

The design can account observed foreground GC/compilation spans on a shared monotonic clock, locate late compilation activity and supply owning main-thread stack samples. It cannot prove the cause of the earlier failed A/A measurements, establish steady state from six passes, estimate unbiased profiler overhead, qualify a new timing method, attribute all processCPU to VM threads, or establish an optimization benefit. Both independent within-policy traces must be reported even if one is quiet or incomplete. A failure to reproduce unusual activity is inconclusive; there is no automatic second campaign.

If root requires a causal GC/JIT-versus-host identification rather than this bounded event-accounting question, REJECT this proposal: four instrumented processes are insufficient for that claim without further interventions/independent controls. In particular, JITless or heap-size interventions would alter workload semantics and cannot be interpreted against the failed baseline by simply comparing ratios.

Barrett's VM warmup results motivate observing the declared full sequence, not assuming steady state. Kalibera/Jones motivate retaining independent processes:1800 calls do not replace four executions. Neither paper diagnoses this Node renderer, and no changepoint inference is proposed.
